detailed_analysis: The fitted band centers are 135/142 (a co-located pair modeling one dominant sharp mode near ~142-144), 391/395 (co-located pair modeling one mode near ~395-399), 514, 636, and 795 cm^-1, with weak features previously near 197 and 305 now absorbed into flank components. This positional pattern is a near-textbook match to ANATASE TiO2: Eg(1) ~144 (strongest), Eg ~197 (weak), B1g ~399, A1g+B1g overlapping ~513-519, and Eg(3) ~639. The measured centers (142/144, ~395, 514, 636) fall within a few cm^-1 of anatase reference positions; the ~399 mode being fit near 391-395 and the 515/639 modes are all consistent. The dominant, very sharp ~144 band with the four weaker companions and NO band near 447/612 (rutile) and NO broad 660-670 (magnetite) strongly favors anatase over other TiO2 polymorphs. The weak, broad ~795 component has no strong anatase counterpart and is most likely a second-order feature, an overtone/combination band, or a minor impurity; its parameters are poorly constrained (center_err 1.4, fwhm_err 5.4). The flat baseline (~3.9% area fraction) and sharp Lorentzian-Gaussian mixed lineshapes are fully consistent with a crystalline oxide with good phonon coherence. The large apex residuals arise because at ~350k counts the Poisson noise is tiny, so even sub-percent lineshape error registers as many sigma; this is a normalization artifact, not evidence of a missing band. Element-consistency: no chemistry (EDX/XRF) was provided, so this is a PATTERN-ONLY identification. Machine-readable band summary (center cm^-1 : relative intensity, strongest first): 142:1.00, 514:0.54, 395:0.40(sum of 391/395 pair ~0.75), 639:0.081, 795:0.016, plus weak ~197 region. The strongest three bands (144, 515, 399) are all explained by anatase.

scientific_claims.claim: The Raman spectrum matches anatase TiO2, with the dominant Eg mode at 142.1 ± 0.01 cm^-1 (FWHM 8.5 ± 0.08 cm^-1) and companion modes at 395 ± 0.06, 514.4 ± 0.03, and 636.4 ± 0.16 cm^-1.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Confident phase identification of a crystalline titania polymorph from vibrational fingerprint alone; the sharp, narrow Eg(1) linewidth indicates well-crystallized, low-defect anatase, relevant to photocatalyst and pigment characterization.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed anatase TiO2 with an Eg(1) mode at ~142 cm^-1 and FWHM near 8.5 cm^-1 as a marker of crystallite quality and phase purity?

model_type: Sum of 7 symmetric pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat (constant) baseline; full-range fit (91-1286 cm^-1) via staged Trust Region Reflective least squares. Reseeded 128/141 shoulder+main pair and 375/394 flank+main pair with min-separation >=9 cm^-1 soft constraint. Baseline area fraction ~0.039 (rolling-min estimate) -> flat baseline used, no ALS.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 7 pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat (constant, near-zero) baseline. Components at approximately: 140, 195, 305, 394, 515, 636, 792 cm⁻¹. Each band appears symmetric in the zoom views, so symmetric pseudo-Voigt (Gaussian/Lorentzian mixture) is appropriate; no asymmetric profile is warranted unless residuals show dispersive S-shapes.

issues.problem: The dominant peak is fit with a single symmetric pseudo-Voigt (FWHM ~11) that is too narrow to capture the broad shoulder on the low-frequency side while simultaneously missing the sharp top; the residual shows a large coherent oscillation (2 sign-changes, +903σ, ±30000 counts).

The strong ~394 peak is under-resolved: the fit's single symmetric profile cannot follow the steep rising edge (~360–395) and the asymmetric fall-off, producing a repeated residual oscillation (3 sign-changes on the rise, 1 on the fall, ±10000 counts).
Residual diagnostics indicate strongly structured (not white) residuals: lag-1 autocorrelation 0.99, global RMS 130× noise, 93.9% of points beyond 3σ.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Reseed the two spurious/near-degenerate components (peak_2, peak_3) as additional profiles on the under-resolved flanks — one near ~128 cm^-1 (low-frequency shoulder of peak 1) and one near ~375 cm^-1 (rising edge of peak 4) — then refit within the 7-component model.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 7 symmetric pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat (constant, near-zero) baseline. The 7 components are retained in count, but two previously spurious/near-degenerate components (former peak_2 at ~196 and peak_3 at ~301) are repurposed as physically meaningful shoulder/flank components. Updated component centers (approximate): ~128 (low-frequency shoulder of the dominant 141 band), ~141 (main sharp band), ~375 (rising-flank component of the 394 band), ~394 (main strong band), ~515, ~636, ~792 cm^-1. All bands remain symmetric pseudo-Voigt (Gaussian/Lorentzian mixture); no asymmetric profiles are introduced. The apparent asymmetry of the 141 and 394 features is now modeled as the superposition of two adjacent symmetric pseudo-Voigts rather than by any single dispersive/skewed lineshape.
